changes.text:
What changed
• One header row: month · ‹ Today › · settings. Subtitle removed; Today shows only when you leave today.
• Today = the tray icon unfolded: coral tile with a darker top band.
• Flat weekend band instead of heavy rounded columns. Six fixed rows, so the window never jumps.
• Agenda: all-day chips, time ranges, Now / in 3 h on today, past events dimmed, empty day links to the next event.
• Click an event: it expands in place with time and duration, location, calendar, Copy and Open ↗.
• Settings: Fluent selector bar (one cue), cards, 40 px rows, one-track weekday picker, keycap shortcut field, no Read-only pill, Close only.
• New icons: coral app tile and coral live-date tile (see the Icons page).
Try it: click days, events, arrows, Today, the settings tabs and About.

slint.text:
Owner decisions, 1 Nov 2026
• Approved: darker coral band on Today and the icons (#A92A31 / #B02E35).
• Approved: Mica backdrop on Windows 11 as optional; needs a Slint/DWM prototype.
• Approved: expandable event details with Copy and Open in provider (Google / Outlook web; hidden for ICS).
• Windows only: macOS dropped from the design.
• Approved 2 Nov: a − button after Settings hides the popup to the tray, like Escape.
• Approved 2 Nov: on the current day the month arrows sit together (‹ ›); leaving it slides them apart and fades Today in between (180 ms, ease-in-out).
Build notes: solid fills, rounded rects, one clip, 1–2 px borders, no blur. Window corners and shadow come from DWM.

datesize-spec.text:
Owner decision, 2 Nov 2026: Date size setting
• Standard 14 px: 34 × 28 tile, 32 px rows, popup 352 × 432.
• Large 16 px: same tile, rows and popup.
• Larger 18 px: 30 px tile, 34 px rows, popup 352 × 444; the agenda keeps its height.
• Only day numbers grow; dots stay 2 px above the tile bottom and the number keeps a 3 px gap above them.
• Windows display scale multiplies all of it: Large at 150 % draws 24 px dates.
• The boards place digits with browser text metrics; Slint draws them about a pixel lower. The app snapshots (calendar-large-light.png, calendar-larger-*.png) are the pixel reference.

local-spec.text:
Stage 2 design, 4 Nov 2026 (ADR 0017)
• Entry points: right-click a day (selects it, opens the editor), + in the agenda header, N (calendar view, no field focused, no dialog; n or N, no Ctrl or Alt), Add event on an empty day. Over the limits or unavailable, each opens a short explanation instead of the editor.
• The editor replaces the agenda; the grid and the 352 × 432 popup stay. Visual and Tab order: Title, All day, Start, End, Location, Note, Save, Cancel. The footer stays pinned; the fields scroll.
• The date is the selected day. Clicking a day while editing moves the event; its tile gets a 1 px outline.
• Enter saves from single-line fields. In Note, Enter adds a line and Ctrl+Enter saves. Esc cancels: the root Escape handler needs an editor-open guard.
• 24-hour HH:MM. Start 00:00–23:59, end 00:01–24:00 and after start; 24:00 stays 24:00 on the same date.
• Save shows errors under their fields and focuses the first one. Limit errors sit above the footer.
• Local details: note, On this PC · Local, then Copy · Edit · Delete on their own line. Delete asks in the row; focus starts on Cancel. Provider rows keep Copy · Open.
• All-day chips become buttons, so local all-day events open the same details.
• Accounts: On this PC is the first card (#0F766E), checked by default. With no account, Connect an account follows it.
• Notices: quiet line, amber strip and red box, as for providers. Start over only for NewerVersion, Damaged and Unreadable.

local-questions.text:
For the owner
1. Save · Cancel follows the ADR order (Save first, the Windows dialog order). The ICS board puts the primary button last; one order should win.
2. No date field: the grid picks the date. A keyboard user changes it by cancelling and selecting another day. Add a date stepper?
3. Show in folder opens Explorer at the kept file. It is small but not in the ADR.
4. The legacy Windows calendars provider shows ‘On this PC’ as its detail line. Rename it so two rows never share that label.
5. The Accounts footnote becomes ‘Accounts are read-only. Only events on this PC can be edited.’
6. Restored, delete-only and unavailable also show a strip at the top of the agenda, since most people never open Settings.
Build notes: solid fills, rounded rects, 1–2 px borders, no blur.
